data.narrative:
Summit Lithium Technologies is a Series A-stage frontier climate and energy company founded by Amanda Hall that has raised approximately C$120M to date. The relevant peer universe comprises one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private competitors in the Climate & Energy sector, including notable names such as Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

Given the nascency of the comparable set and absence of sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage peers meeting minimum density thresholds, the Peer-Median method was not applicable. Instead, valuation relies on the Stage-Progression approach, which applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to the C$120M capital raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $240M. This method captures the expected value increase between rounds absent a sufficiently dense peer dataset for direct market benchmarking.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $204M to $276M, centered at $240M. The spread reflects inherent uncertainty in the stage-progression multiplier and the absence of granular comparable transaction data within the narrow Climate & Energy lithium technology segment. Key uncertainties include whether the 2.0x multiplier appropriately reflects current market conditions for Series A climate tech, and the degree to which broader sector peers are truly comparable to Summit's specific technology and market positioning. A more precise valuation would benefit from additional same-stage private transactions or a denser set of publicly traded lithium technology comparables.
